subject: MSA & Order Form — consumer product rights, training constraints, and feedback license negotiation
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@appspark.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@appspark.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on training rights + downstream productization

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the demo last week. Procurement attached our MSA redlines (see AppSpark_MSA_redline_v3.pdf). Two items blocking internal sign-off:

1) Training/use of customer content — we need explicit assurance that any use of our customer data for model training is opt-in, with a mechanism to exclude production traffic.
2) Downstream productization — legal is concerned that "unrestricted output use" could allow Redwood or partners to resurface AppSpark-specific prompts or features into other customer-facing products.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: opt-in training only vs a feedback license; whether outputs attributable to AppSpark users will be considered AppSpark property; and any telemetry/telemetry retention rules?

If helpful, procurement is available for an hour on Tuesday the 30th to walk through redlines.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Head of Product Ops
AppSpark

Attachments: AppSpark_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 82KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@appspark.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on training rights + downstream productization

Maria — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (Customer Success) so we can respond precisely. Quick summary of Redwood's current posture:

- Feedback/training license: the standard MSA gives Redwood a narrow feedback license to improve service quality (aggregate, de-identified). We do not claim ownership of customer outputs.
- Opt-in training: we can support an opt-in for training ("no-training" default) for customers who require it, with an addendum covering allowed data subsets and duration.
- Downstream productization: Redwood will not rebrand or export AppSpark-specific prompts as AppSpark's property; however, we do reserve the right to use aggregated learnings and model improvements that are not identifiable to any single customer.

Next steps: Laura — can you confirm whether the language in Section 6.2 of the attached PDF can be revised to reflect the opt-in option and tighter de-identification guarantees? Maria — happy to join procurement on Tue 30th at 11:00 PT.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@appspark.com>, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Questions on training rights + downstream productization

Maria — thanks for raising the specifics. A few clarifications and proposed edits we intend to offer: 

1) Training / Feedback license: propose a two-tier approach in the MSA: (A) default "service improvement" license limited to aggregate, de-identified signals and model telemetry; (B) a separate training addendum customers may sign to allow use of non-production, sampled data for targeted model fine-tuning. The addendum will specify: sampling rate, retention window, and strict access controls.

2) Opt-out and production exclusion: we will add a clear clause and a technical control so AppSpark can mark production endpoints as opt-out ("no-train") at the route level. This will be honored within 24 hours of flagging.

3) Output ownership / downstream uses: we will revise the output clause to say: AppSpark retains ownership of Customer Outputs; Redwood retains a right to use de-identified aggregated learnings for product improvement, but Redwood will not sell or sublicense AppSpark-specific outputs to third parties nor incorporate identifiable AppSpark prompts as standalone features.

4) Auditability & telemetry retention: propose a 180-day retention for request/response logs in the hosted offering by default; longer retention available under Dedicated/Private contracts. We can provide sampling-based logs and an audit package for procurement review.

I will redline Section 6 and 9 and circulate v4 of the MSA. If AppSpark wants contract language for the addendum today, I can draft it and share as well.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will send redline PDF in follow-up)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@appspark.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@appspark.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:53:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on training rights + downstream productization

Laura — that two-tier approach sounds promising. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we can move: 

- If we sign the training addendum, we need a firm commitment that AppSpark-specific prompt templates and any derived business logic will not be surfaced in general Redwood model releases. We understand aggregated improvements, but need an explicit carve-out.
- What counts as "de-identified" in your view? We need an assurance that small identifiers (like internal product names, internal endpoints, or recurring user phrases) will be treated as PII and excluded from training.
- Can you confirm the turnaround for honoring opt-out flags at scale? Our SRE team is nervous about the 24-hour window for very high-throughput routes.

Procurement asked whether you can provide a short legal summary (one page) that we can give to our VP Legal and procurement to enable an expedited approval. We also put a soft timeline of needing signed docs by Dec 20 to get Q1 rollout.

Thanks — Maria

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@appspark.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on training rights + downstream productization

Maria — following up with specifics to help your procurement/legal team decide quickly. Short answers below and attached a one-page summary we prepared for similar deals.

- Carve-out for AppSpark-specific templates: yes — the training addendum will include a prohibition on incorporating AppSpark prompt templates or business logic into any commercial model feature set. We will also add language requiring Redwood to notify AppSpark before any release that leverages customer-contributed data beyond aggregate signals.

- Definition of de-identification: we will adopt NIST-inspired de-id guidance — remove direct identifiers and apply token-based suppression for recurring sequence patterns that clearly map to AppSpark internals. We cannot guarantee perfect removal for unconstrained natural language, but we will agree to a remediation workflow if AppSpark identifies derivations that appear in released models.

- Opt-out turnaround: we can commit to sub-6-hour propagation for Dedicated customers; for hosted customers we will guarantee 24 hours. For AppSpark (per your scale), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to meet the SRE needs — we will include operational SLA language in the Order Form.

Attached: one-page-legal-summary_AppSpark_RDW.pdf; updated OrderForm_AppSpark_2026-11-30.docx (with Dedicated option and training addendum checkbox). Please confirm if that timeline (sign by Dec 20) still works. Happy to jump on a final 30-minute call with VP Legal if that helps.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: one-page-legal-summary_AppSpark_RDW.pdf, OrderForm_AppSpark_2026-11-30.docx
